text.title: Product Launch Procedure
text.summary: Step-by-step procedure to apply Product Launch end-to-end. Each step names its input, action, and output.

step.name: t-minus-timeline
step.action: Use the T-minus framework: T-8 weeks (strategy finalized), T-6 (asset creation begins), T-4 (audience building), T-2 (all assets ready), T-1 (final checks), T-Day (execute), T+1 (monitor), T+2 (retrospective).
step.output: Dated milestone plan with an owner per asset (r11-asset-floor)
step.note: Without a structured timeline, asset creation and coordination compress into the last 2 weeks, producing rushed copy, missed channels, and support unpreparedness.

step.name: position
step.action: Author the one-page positioning: primary segment, the alternative it displaces, the value claim. One segment, one message.
step.decision-gate: If more than one segment is named as primary, stop — pick, and file the rest as derivative angles.

step.name: pre-launch
step.action: Build assets, brief support, arm monitors, draft the per-channel day-of runbook with timestamps, owners and reversal steps.

step.name: dry-run
step.action: Walk the day-of timeline through with each named owner and verify the core user flows by hand before any flag is flipped.
step.decision-gate: A flow that fails here is fixed quietly; the same failure found after the email blast needs a public correction.

step.name: launch-day
step.action: Release, announce per-segment cadence, watch monitors live.

step.name: first-72h
step.action: Stand-by for incident response; respond to feedback queue.

step.name: post-launch-review
step.action: Compare to success thresholds; emit scale / hold / rollback decision.

text.reference: Bash script that polls signup and visitor metrics every 5 minutes and posts to a Slack webhook. Run it from step 4 (launch-day) against the thresholds set under r17-alert-thresholds.
